gaps: P0: nothing (#1 is a saint, not a view); P3: nothing (#10–#11 are Brascassat landscapes of Italy); P5: Mittelholzer aerials show mostly fields and the airfield
notes: #5: Chastillon died about 1616; 1641 is the Topographie françoise edition date in the BnF record; faint center fold, not a book gutter. #8 is dated only to Neyts’s working life (1643–87); drop it if that range is too loose. #6 (Duviert 1610) is a poor microfilm-like scan with a gutter. #2–#4 are London, Metz and Nîmes; #12 is Châlons. #13 (1890s town hall photochrom) and #16 (Barau 1894) are alternatives for P4. #22 is the only usable modern photo; the others are street scenes.
